projects.title: Zendtri - Multi-Tenant Retail Operations Platform
projects.metaDescription: A multi-tenant retail operations platform for Philippine SMEs — covering point of sale, inventory, purchasing, workforce, expenses, customer programs, online ordering, and subscription billing across web, iOS, and Android.
responsibilities: Organization-scoped access controls via PostgreSQL row-level policies
Server-authoritative inventory math via SQL RPC functions
MVVM architecture across separate desktop and mobile views
Cross-platform delivery to web, iOS, and Android via Capacitor
projects.shortDescription: Zendtri is a multi-tenant retail operations platform for Philippine SMEs. I designed and built the product across point of sale, inventory, purchasing, workforce, expenses, customer programs, online ordering, and subscription billing—delivered across web, iOS, and Android.

meta.scope: Product · UX · Web · Mobile · Backend · Data
meta.builtFor: Philippine SMEs — retail shops, cafés, and food stalls

requirements: Selling: POS terminal (desktop, tablet-landscape, and mobile layouts), promotions, transactions and receipts
Inventory: items, categories, stock levels, purchase orders, branch-to-branch stock transfers, low-stock alerts, barcode and label printing
Management: multi-branch, users and roles, customers, suppliers, cash management, activity and audit log
Reporting: sales reports, dashboards, PDF and Excel export
Billing: subscription plans, PayMongo checkout, plan-gated feature limits
projects.overview: Zendtri is a multi-tenant retail operations platform for Philippine SMEs. I designed and built the product across point of sale, inventory, purchasing, workforce, expenses, customer programs, online ordering, and subscription billing—delivered across web, iOS, and Android.
projects.challenge: Off-the-shelf POS tools are usually either too expensive and enterprise-heavy for a neighborhood café, or too simplistic to handle real inventory — unit conversions, recipe-based deduction, multi-branch stock transfers. Filipino SMEs needed something that handles multiple branches under one business without data bleeding between them, gets inventory math right (buying flour by the sack but selling bread by the piece), supports local payment rails and peso pricing, scales cost via self-serve subscription tiers, and works on any device.
projects.approach: A single React and TypeScript application, backed by Supabase, shipped to web and to app stores via Capacitor. The core engineering focus was on three systems that had to be correct, not just functional: organization-scoped access controls, server-authoritative inventory, and plan-based feature gating. Organization-scoped access is enforced through PostgreSQL row-level policies, keeping each tenant's data isolated at the database. Every quantity-affecting transform — unit conversion, recipe deduction, sale creation — runs inside SQL functions on the server, keeping the sale, sale_items, payments, and inventory-movement chain consistent. Subscription plans store capabilities as JSONB feature flags and numeric limits, and the server re-validates every limit and returns HTTP 402 if a request slips past the client gates — so re-tiering a feature is a data change rather than a code deploy.

results.description: Branches, staff roles, permissions, and organization-scoped workflows.

results.title: Inventory Engine
results.description: Weighted-average costing, recipes, stock counts, transfers, wastage, and inventory controls.

results.title: End-to-End Commerce
results.description: Point of sale, purchasing, customers, payments, reporting, and online ordering.

results.title: Web · iOS · Android
results.description: One product experience delivered across web and mobile platforms.

projects.conclusion: Zendtri ships as one React and TypeScript codebase to web, iOS, and Android, with organization-scoped access enforced in PostgreSQL, all inventory math computed server-side in SQL, and subscription features gated by data-driven JSONB plan flags rather than code deploys. The result is a retail operations platform where correctness lives at the database layer — a single source of truth that stays consistent across every client and form factor.

projects.overview: Hunter Vault is a personal finance app that reimagines budgeting as an RPG adventure, inspired by the Solo Leveling universe. Instead of spreadsheets and boring dashboards, users manage their financial life through quests, ranks, and a vault system — making money management engaging, motivating, and habit-forming. projects.challenge: Most budgeting apps fail because they're boring — users open them once and never return. The core challenge was building a finance tool that people actually want to use daily. A second constraint was doing this without compromising privacy: no ads, no data collection, no account lock-in. Building an engaging gamification layer on top of real financial logic while keeping the app fully offline required a fundamentally different architecture from typical finance apps.
projects.approach: Hunter Vault was designed around a single insight: people who game consistently show up every day because the progression loop is rewarding. By mapping financial behaviors to RPG mechanics — income as XP, debt as dungeon raids, savings goals as quests — the app makes responsible financial habits feel like meaningful progression. The rank system (E to S+) gives users a clear visual sense of growth over time. Going fully offline with no account requirement removed the biggest barrier to entry: trust. Users never have to wonder who holds their financial data.

projects.overview: Hero Journals is a web app designed to help traders log, analyze, and improve their trading performance. It provides a structured system to track trades, evaluate strategies, and monitor trading psychology over time, with a focus on usability, automation, and insightful analytics.
projects.challenge: Traditionally, retail traders managed their trading records in Excel and Google Sheets. While this method was functional, it lacked automation, analytical depth, and real-time insights. Manual data entry was both time-consuming and prone to errors, making it difficult to maintain accuracy. Additionally, they had no consolidated view of key performance metrics such as win rate, risk/reward ratio, and drawdown. Tracking trade psychology and decision-making patterns was also challenging, and the fragmented data made it nearly impossible to identify recurring mistakes or capitalize on consistent strengths.
projects.approach:
Retail traders adopted Hero Journals, a digital platform designed for active traders seeking deeper insight into their performance and decision-making processes. The platform provided a more efficient and organized alternative to his previous manual tracking methods. 
 One of the key features retail traders benefited from was the automatic trade import functionality, which allowed him to seamlessly upload data from brokerage CSVs and APIs. This eliminated the need for manual entry and ensured that his records were always up to date. 
 The app also enabled retail traders to use custom tags and notes to track specific strategies, emotional states, and trade setups. This helped them analyze not just the outcomes of their trades, but also the reasoning and mindset behind each decision. 
 Interactive dashboards provided a clear visual representation of his performance, displaying metrics such as profit and loss trends, average risk/reward ratios, and maximum drawdowns. These insights made it easier for traders to assess his trading edge and refine his approach. 
 Additionally, the app's searchable trade history allowed traders to filter and review trades based on setups, strategies, or results, making post-trade analysis faster and more effective. With built-in goal tracking and journaling tools, he was also able to monitor his progress over time and stay accountable to his trading discipline.

projects.title: Transforming Workforce Management with Face Recognition-Based Payroll and Attendance Software
projects.metaDescription: This solution is a web based application built using ReactJS and Laravel for the backend. It is also mobile friendly so users can access the attendance face recognition using mobile device.
projects.shortDescription: 7th Grocery Store implemented a face recognition-based payroll and attendance system to eliminate manual tracking, reduce time fraud, and automate payroll processing. The solution combined AI-powered facial recognition, mobile attendance for remote workers, real-time dashboards, and GPS validation to streamline HR operations across multiple locations.
requirements: Face Recognition Login: 98.9% accurate detection under varied lighting and with masks
Real-Time Sync: Instant updates to a centralized cloud system across all locations
Auto Payroll Calculation: Overtime, late arrivals, and leaves are automatically computed
Audit Trail & Reporting: Generates monthly reports, audit logs, and compliance summaries
Secure Data Handling: GDPR & ISO 27001 compliant infrastructure
projects.overview:
7th Grocery Store embarked on a digital transformation initiative to modernize its workforce management by implementing a face recognition-based payroll and attendance system. The project aimed to replace outdated manual processes with a smart, automated solution that would enhance accuracy, eliminate time fraud, and streamline payroll operations. 
 The solution integrated AI-powered facial recognition technology with real-time attendance tracking, automated payroll calculations, and centralized HR reporting. By leveraging biometric authentication, the system ensured secure and tamper-proof attendance records while significantly reducing administrative overhead. The project covered over 20+ employees across three store locations, including provisions for remote and field staff through a mobile face scan app. 
 This strategic implementation not only addressed key operational pain points but also positioned 7thgrocery as a forward-thinking employer investing in transparency, efficiency, and employee satisfaction.
projects.challenge:
7thgrocery Store was grappling with significant inefficiencies in its workforce management system. The company relied on manual attendance tracking methods, including paper logs and ID cards, which frequently resulted in data entry errors and inconsistencies. One of the most pressing issues was the prevalence of buddy punching—where employees clocked in or out on behalf of their colleagues—leading to inflated labor costs and a lack of accountability. 
 Additionally, the payroll process was heavily manual, requiring over five days of HR effort each month to compile, verify, and process employee data. This not only strained the HR department but also delayed salary disbursements and created dissatisfaction among employees. Compounding these challenges was the lack of real-time visibility into attendance across multiple factory locations, which made workforce oversight and decision-making increasingly difficult. Collectively, these issues hampered productivity, compromised compliance, and eroded trust in the company's time and attendance system.
projects.approach:
To address the challenges faced by 7th Grocery Store, we deployed an integrated Face Recognition-Based Payroll and Attendance System designed for accuracy, automation, and scalability. At the core of the solution were AI-powered face recognition terminals installed at all entry and exit points. These terminals enabled fast, secure, and contactless employee identification, significantly reducing errors and eliminating the possibility of buddy punching. 
 To accommodate remote and field employees, a mobile face scan application was introduced, allowing them to log attendance securely from any location. A real-time attendance dashboard was also implemented, giving HR personnel and department heads instant visibility into workforce data across all locations. 
 The system was further enhanced with an automated payroll module that synced seamlessly with attendance records, enabling precise calculation of working hours, overtime, and deductions. Leave management was also integrated, ensuring that all approved leaves were factored into the final payroll. For the mobile workforce, geo-fencing and GPS-based logging features were added to validate attendance locations and enhance accountability. Together, these components created a comprehensive, automated system that revolutionized how 7Th Grocery manages time, attendance, and payroll.

projects.overview: Japanese Candlestick Patterns was developed to fill a critical gap in the trading education market: the lack of accessible, practical tools for learning candlestick patterns. projects.challenge: Many beginner traders struggle to understand candlestick patterns, often relying on scattered online resources or overwhelming textbooks. projects.approach: To meet the educational needs of aspiring traders, the development team created a comprehensive candlestick pattern learning app packed with powerful and user-friendly features. At the core of the app are interactive learning modules that break down over 40 bullish and bearish candlestick patterns into bite-sized, easy-to-understand lessons. These patterns range from simple forms like doji and hammer to more complex ones like engulfing patterns and the three white soldiers. To ensure users can apply what they learn, the app includes multi-level quizzes to test and exercise the patterns that they learned.

projects.conclusion: Japanese Candlestick Patterns successfully transformed complex financial education into an accessible, interactive, and enjoyable experience. By focusing on user engagement, practical skills, and adaptive learning, the app empowered thousands of aspiring traders to master candlestick charting—equipping them with essential tools for smarter trading decisions.
